body:
Thanks @Yuren0312. I independently reproduced the original head and a local merge with current master (6f571f8): new tests 16/16, market suite 41/41, full npm test 314/314. Your native Node command genuinely reports market.ts line coverage 98.74% (branch 93.98%); the repository's npm run test:cov protocol reports market.ts 98.99% and overall 95.37%, both above the existing 85% gate. These are different instrumentation protocols, so I am keeping the figures separate. The same-protocol repository baseline is 69.85%, rather than treating the August 69.6% as a new measurement.

I approved the first-time external-contributor Actions run; all five jobs now pass: https://github.com/pengpengyi92/dsh-quant/actions/runs/39112195592 . There is no current content conflict. An offline sentinel probe also verified that all 16 tests restore fetch and make zero unmocked fetch attempts under the repository's default serial-per-file test execution.

One required correction before merge: the mock input uses the DOM-only RequestInfo name, which fails an explicit Node-only TypeScript check (TS2552). Existing npm typecheck/CI is green because tsconfig.json includes src only and the compatibility script check does not include this new file. The one-line runtime-derived type suggested inline passes that explicit check and preserves 16/16 tests in a local probe. This is not a claim that npm test currently fails.

I also left a non-blocking assertion-strength follow-up: the five native uncovered lines are safeFetch's shared network/HTTP error paths, and the Binance truncation test currently checks only the prefix. This does not invalidate the measured coverage or your provider-dispatch work. No production changes or fork rewrite are needed for the requested type correction. Keeping #106 open until the reviewed head is corrected and accepted; your original commit and authorship will be retained.
